newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank of Canada sells Canadian dollars - traders.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Canada sells Canadian dollars - traders.

text.p: The Bank of Canada intervened and sold Canadian dollars for U.S. dollars as the currency traded around the C$1.3828 level, dealers said.
The intervention was through brokers and considered moderate as the currency strengthened through key resistance.
Following the intervention, the Canadian dollar was trading at C$1.3822 after opening at C$1.3846 and Wednesday's close of C$1.3893. Traders expect further gains.
The Bank of Canada does not comment on intervention.
Bank intervention came after comments by Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen suggesting that the trend for the Canada dollar was positive.
The bank was sending the signal to the markets that monetary conditions were going to tighten, said Mark Chandler, senior economist with Goldman Sachs. "That is the spark plug for this rally."
